scenarios.name: csv-import-validation
scenarios.rationale: Both responses correctly identify that the CSV file is needed before analysis can proceed, so neither meets the rubric's core requirements (data profile, validation checks with counts/samples, concrete fixes). However, Response A frames a more comprehensive analysis roadmap with 6+ specific validation dimensions (null rates, type consistency, range validity, duplicates, unique values) that directly map to the rubric, while Response B makes more generic promises with less specificity about what will be delivered.

scenarios.name: schema-contract-validation
scenarios.rationale: Both responses appropriately request missing information (analytics data and schema files), but Response B is more aligned with rubric requirements by explicitly describing the validation outputs it will deliver (row counts, affected records, compliance checks, concrete remediation steps), while Response A correctly identifies a context mismatch but offers less detail about the analytics-specific validation approach and output format the rubric expects.

scenarios.name: freshness-and-drift-check
scenarios.rationale: A requests data without attempting analysis despite files being visible in the user's working directory, failing all rubric requirements; B analyzes actual staleness (112 fresh vs 199 stale, 9-day gap) and identifies quality degradation patterns (documentation-only verifications, uncertain entries, line bloat) but uses non-standard quality metrics and only partially formalizes alert thresholds rather than specifying numeric rules.
